correctness.rationale: PASS: Rebuilt R_s=(I-sQ)^(-1) as the cyclic geometric resolvent with r=s/(1+s), C=2R_s-I. Differentiating R_s gives C^2=I+4sR_s prime and every off-diagonal coefficient has sign of jS_n-rS_n prime; j=1 is the sharp one, F_n. The diagonal of C^2 is strictly positive from the circulant product. F_n decreases with the unique n>=4 root and limiting r=1/2. For fixed odd k, s->infinity gives C^k->2J/n-I, with negative diagonal for n>=3. For even k=2m>=2 and n>=4, its adjacent coefficient is -2m(n-3)/(ns)+O(s^(-2)), hence negative for large s. Direct independent sympy inversions/matrix powers tested 84 small n/r and high-s k cases; exact h=4 n=3 and n=4 witnesses reproduced. The analytical asymptotic, not finite experiments, handles unbounded h and all k.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge original classification of entrywise nonnegative fixed powers of the unfiltered Crank–Nicolson Cayley map on a unit-rate directed finite cycle. The generic M-matrix/Cayley identity and the one-step resolvent return test are prior work. The new point is that the *square* is positive at every step on the oriented three-cycle, every even power shares that exception, and for n>=4 the exact two-step boundary is a unique cyclic polynomial zero while every fixed power fails at sufficiently large step. No broader result inspected implies this parity classification.
residual_risks: An underindexed theorem about eventual nonnegativity, positive powers of Cayley transforms, or nonreversible Markov matrices might contain this special classification.

value.rationale: PASS: Entrywise positivity is mandatory for a Markov transition approximation to avoid negative probabilities. A negative Crank–Nicolson single step followed by a second equal step is genuinely recoverable for the directed three-cycle at every step size, while the exact dimension-four and higher cutoff proves the boundary of this mechanism. This gives a motivated parity/dimension classification and sharp step-size frontier rather than routine verification of a named small matrix.

final_claim: For n>=2 unit-rate oriented cycle Q=P-I and integer k>=1, (I-hQ/2)^(-1)(I+hQ/2) to power k is nonnegative for every h>0 precisely if n=2 or n=3 with k even. For n>=4, the nonnegative second-power interval ends at H_n=2rho_n/(1-rho_n) where F_n(rho_n)=1-sum_{j=2}^{n-1}(j-1)rho_n^j=0, with H_n decreasing to 2.
limitations: Unit-rate single oriented finite cycle, fixed equal time step and fixed exponent k. No claim for general Markov generators, variable rates/steps or stage positivity.
Results on finite n and s grid independently corroborate but cannot certify all real step sizes or powers.
Equivalent underindexed Cayley power positivity literature remains possible.
